targets.approach: Follow the signs toward Sunrise; the Salamander wall appears on your left. The route is the fourth on the wall, starting in an obvious crack system.
targets.name: Bitches Brew

targets.approach: Follow the signs toward Sunrise; the Salamander wall appears on your left. The route starts up a short crack and climbs the stepped arete above.
targets.name: Hobbit Step

targets.approach: Follow the signs toward Sunrise; the Salamander wall appears on your left. This is the first route you reach, starting up an obvious crack.
targets.name: Midnight Sun

targets.approach: The route begins from Cairn Cabin by climbing the glacier to the Footstool, the feature at the foot of the steep east ridge. Access to the Sir Sandford group is long, with several sub-ranges between it and the Rogers Pass area.
targets.name: East Ridge

targets.approach: Continue past the main wall at Skid Row and Skid Row West is up and on the left on the way to Sunrise. Past Put Away Wet, the route is the striking crack set back in a small alcove.
targets.name: Come On Jam

targets.approach: Take the third pullout on the way toward Gold River and follow the trail into the rocky river bed. The Sluice Wall is just right of the Joint Wall, where a trail goes up stairs on the right. The route is the obvious crack system behind a fallen log.
targets.descent_text: The top can be walked off.
targets.name: Sluicebox Crack

targets.approach: Overlook Mountain is in the Triple Peaks group of the South Powell Divide. Drive up Goat Main to the foot of the Goat 2 forest road and follow it until it bends onto an old bushy road, then find the flagging into open forest on the right. An old trail leads up through dense bush to the south ridge, which begins right where the forest ends.
targets.descent_text: Descend the northwest ridge to a key ledge that gives easy access into the bowl below the south ridge, then follow along the ridge back to the bush.
targets.name: Overlook Mt south ridge

targets.approach: It lies in the Skwim Mt area, at the top of the Stillwater main road. Hike up the Skwim trail, climb the boulder field directly, then contour left beneath the Boot to reach the north ridge, then walk the ridge to the base of the route.
targets.descent_text: A tree at the top serves as a belay for the second and as a rappel anchor; rappelling is the alternative to the dense, bushy south face route.
targets.name: The Boot North ridge

targets.approach: The approach to Tantalus crosses the Dione Glacier from the hut, and the climb needs a screw or a picket for the bergschrund.
targets.name: Tantalus Standard Route

targets.approach: The Big Scoop Wall is the broad granite basin on the southeast face of Habrich West, reached by Al's Habrich Ridge trail or another trail up the ridge. From Habrich West's summit, descend its south side and curve around toward the wall; the Glenn's Gangway trail also leads to its base. This is the right-most route on the wall. It starts on a smaller horizontal fault on the lower scoop, in a brushy corner beside a tilted dead tree, and a single bolt marks the start.
targets.name: Chocolate Chip

targets.approach: The Big Scoop Wall is the broad granite basin on the southeast face of Habrich West, reached by Al's Habrich Ridge trail or another trail up the ridge. From Habrich West's summit, descend its south side and curve around toward the wall; the Glenn's Gangway trail also leads to its base. The route starts on the second horizontal fault, a broad sandy ledge, at a one bolt in a little corner under a dark streak.
targets.name: Creme Caramel

targets.approach: The Big Scoop Wall is the broad granite basin on the southeast face of Habrich West, reached by Al's Habrich Ridge trail or another trail up the ridge. From Habrich West's summit, descend its south side and curve around toward the wall; the Glenn's Gangway trail also leads to its base. The route starts at the end of the sandy, vegetated ledge, just right of Creme Caramel, at a single bolt.
targets.name: Rocky Road

targets.approach: The Big Scoop Wall is the broad granite basin on the southeast face of Habrich West, reached by Al's Habrich Ridge trail or another trail up the ridge. From Habrich West's summit, descend its south side and curve around toward the wall; the Glenn's Gangway trail also leads to its base. Tiramisu is the left-most route: reach the large treed ledge that cuts across the upper wall from its left side, and start at the end of that ledge above the big trees.
targets.name: Tiramisu

targets.approach: Use the Crown Mountain approach: near Crown's top, veer left and contour around the peak's north side, then go down a fixed line to the foot of the Camel. The route takes the twin cracks at the Camel's neck, with an off-width variation to the left.
targets.name: Camel Cracks

targets.approach: Use the Crown Mountain approach: near Crown's top, veer left and contour around the peak's north side, then go down a fixed line to the foot of the Camel. The route begins in the middle of the Camel's back and traverses right.
targets.name: Hind Leg Route

targets.approach: Use the Crown Mountain approach: near Crown's top, veer left and contour around the peak's north side, then go down a fixed line to the foot of the Camel. The route follows the ridge up the Camel's back at the far right side of the formation.
targets.name: Regular Route

targets.approach: Use the Crown Mountain approach: near Crown's top, veer left and contour around the peak's north side, then go down a fixed line to the foot of the Camel. The route begins by a shrub, a short way beneath where the Camel's hump begins.
targets.descent_text: The top of the route has bolted anchors on the hump's left side.
targets.name: The Hunk

targets.approach: Pull off on the right immediately short of the first tunnel you meet driving east from the Rogers Pass discovery centre. Walk back up the road a short way, cross it, and take the service road to the shed on the far side to the end of the avalanche chute, then follow the chute uphill. The South Tower is the buttress up the Camels' southern side; three tree bands show below it, and pitched climbing starts at a ledge above the third band with orange tat on a tree.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the Tupper-Camel traverse and the lone pine slide.
targets.name: South Tower

targets.approach: Reach the East Creek basin by climbing the Bugaboo Snowpatch Col to the upper Vowell Glacier, crossing toward the Pigeon-Howser Col and descending to the East Creek Glacier. The East Creek bivy is on a rib of rock and scree, a short way below the Minaret. From camp, go directly uphill to the west face's left side. Climb the snow to the first weakness left of the major gash that splits the southwest face; depending on snow level, step across the gap to a sloping ledge to rope up on, or climb a few meters from a crack on the right.
targets.name: Reinhold Pussycat

targets.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Duck a L'Orange takes the left-hand of the three southwest-facing ribs on the central summit (The Contact Zone is on the right and Black September in the middle). It starts across the west couloir from the West Buttress of the South Peak, in steep cracks on polished orange rock.
targets.descent_text: Go down the standard scrambling ramp on the west face, starting from the col between the north and central summits.
targets.name: Duck a L'Orange

targets.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Above Daiphy Lake, climb talus to the col on the south side of the peak, then cross the broad snowfield to its southeast and contour down to the east buttress. The start is among boulders at the north side of the buttress's lower end, beneath a slabby dihedral.
targets.descent_text: Downclimb the third-class ramps on the south ridge's east flank, a fourth-class chimney, and the slabs beyond it.
targets.name: East Buttress of the South Peak

targets.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Mars Western is on the southwest face of the south summit and starts well right of the west buttress's lower end, in steep corners streaked with black.
targets.descent_text: Use the south peak's west-buttress descent, which goes down that peak's south ridge.
targets.name: Mars Western

targets.approach: The Old Settler stands in the Coast Mountains on the east side of Harrison Lake. The usual drive is the Harrison East forest road from Harrison Hot Springs, past Sasquatch Park, then the gravel logging road north to the Bear Creek logging camp. West- and south-facing routes continue by the Talc Creek North road, then a deactivated spur, a bushwhack through the subalpine bowl and a forested headwall to campsites at Daiphy Lake, and from the lake the base is reached over talus. Go by way of Daiphy Lake to the minor rib at the far right of the south peak's southwest face; higher up, the line crosses the gully leftward onto a basalt dyke and joins the crest of the West Buttress.
targets.descent_text: Come down the south peak's south ridge, the way used from the West Buttress.
targets.name: Totally Spurious

targets.approach: Reach it over the Sphinx Glacier by the Castle Towers approach, or paddle the lake to Sphinx Bay and climb from there. Then go up the glacier to the foot of the north ridge. The lower pitches are blocky scrambling, and the proper climbing begins higher up, on cracks that split the slab.
targets.name: North Ridge

targets.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. Helix starts on the left side of the ear on grassy ledges.
targets.descent_text: Descend the gully to the left of the route. It is also the bail-out line, reached by traversing left.
targets.name: Helix

targets.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. The route is a harder finish to Helix: at the top of Helix's fourth pitch, instead of traversing left on the ramp, go right at the lower grade or a little left at the higher one, set a gear belay over a little roof, then take a crack system on to the summit.
targets.name: The Antihelix

targets.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. The line links broken cracks and corners in the gap between Helix and The Gift and begins a little to the right of Helix. Follow the Helix ledge beyond a single boulder and belay shortly past it, beneath a roof.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route on the bolted stations, which have been updated. It is possible to rappel from near the top of the fourth pitch.
targets.name: The Pack
